nodes.summary: For every natural number $n \ge 7$ and every admissible bag $F$ for $n$ people, the weight of $F$ is at least $\frac{n^2}{6} + 2n - \frac{11}{2}$.
nodes.title: Lower bound for the weight of an admissible bag

nodes.summary: For a natural number $n$ and a bag $F$, that is, a finite multiset of finite sets of natural numbers, the weight of $F$ for $n$ people is the real number $w(F) = \sum_{T \in F} \left(\max T + \sum_{i \in T} i\right) - \frac{n(n+1)}{2}$, where each set counts with its multiplicity in $F$ and $\max \emptyset = 0$.
nodes.title: Weight of a bag

nodes.summary: Let $T_3(n)$ be the optimal crossing time of $n$ people with crossing times $1, \dots, n$ on a bridge of capacity $3$ with one torch. For every $n \ge 13$, $T_3(n) = T_3(n - 6) + 2n + 6$.

nodes.title: End vertex of a star movement

nodes.title: Some admissible bag weighs at most the capacity-3 optimal time

nodes.summary: Let $n \ge 1$ and consider the people $1, \dots, n$, person $i$ having crossing time $i$, on a bridge of capacity $3$ with one torch. Then some schedule has total time equal to the optimal crossing time $T_3(n)$ and the following property: every return (a crossing at an odd position, counting from $0$) carries a single person $p$, and $p \le q$ for every person $q$ on the right bank just before that return.
nodes.title: Optimal capacity-3 schedules with fastest single returns

nodes.summary: For the schedule whose crossings are, in order, $\{1,2\}$, $\{1\}$, $\{1,3\}$, $\{1\}$, $\{1,4\}$, the forward crossings are $\{1,2\}, \{1,3\}, \{1,4\}$ and the returns are $\{1\}, \{1\}$. For the people $1, 2, 3, 4$, the right bank after the crossings $\{1,2\}$, $\{1\}$ (the first two of the schedule) is $\{2\}$.
nodes.title: Forward moves, returns and right bank of a four-person schedule

nodes.summary: The forward crossings of a list of crossings are its entries at the even positions $0, 2, 4, \dots$ (counting from $0$), in their original order. For a schedule these are its forward moves, from left to right.
nodes.title: Forward crossings

nodes.summary: Let $n$ be a natural number and let $\sigma$ be a schedule for the people $1, \dots, n$ on a bridge of capacity $3$ in which every return carries exactly one person. Let $F(\sigma)$ be the multiset of the forward crossings of $\sigma$. Then $F(\sigma)$ is an admissible bag for $n$ people, and the total time of $\sigma$ equals the weight $w(F(\sigma))$ of this bag for $n$ people.
nodes.title: Schedules with single-person returns give admissible bags

nodes.summary: The multiset whose only member is the set $\{1, 2, 3\}$ is an admissible bag for $3$ people, and its weight for $3$ people is $3$.

Since person $p$ has crossing time $p$, each crossing costs the largest crossing time among the people in it.
nodes.title: Total time of a schedule

No condition is imposed on $P$ here (it may even be…

A finite sequence $\sigma = (S_1, \dots, S_\ell)$ of steps, each a finite list of movements, is a legal run from the configuration $(\mathrm{pos}, \mathrm{tor})$ when each step $S_i$ is legal from the configuration reached after…

nodes.summary: A step is a finite list of movements carried out in parallel. Its duration is the largest crossing time $p + 1$ of a person $p$ moving in one of its movements, and $0$ if no person moves.

nodes.summary: Given the vertex $\mathrm{pos}(p)$ of each person $p$ and a step $S$, a finite list of movements, the position of $p$ after $S$ is the end vertex of the first movement of $S$ whose persons include $p$ (its leaf if the movement is outward, the center if it is inward), and $\mathrm{pos}(p)$ if no movement of $S$ includes $p$.

nodes.summary: Given the number $\mathrm{tor}(v)$ of torches at each vertex $v$ of the star graph and a step $S$, a finite list of movements, the number of torches at $v$ after $S$ is $\max(\mathrm{tor}(v) - a, 0) + b$, where $a$ is the number of movements of $S$ that start at $v$ and $b$ is the number of movements of $S$ that end at $v$.

nodes.title: Bridge and torch on star graphs

nodes.summary: Let $T(n, k, t)$ be the optimal time of the star model with $n$ persons, $k$ edges and $t$ torches. For every star schedule $\sigma$ with $n$ persons, $k$ edges and $t$ torches, $T(n, k, t)$ is at most the total duration of $\sigma$, the sum of the durations of its steps.
nodes.title: Every star schedule bounds the optimal time

nodes.summary: For $n$ persons, $k$ edges and $t$ torches, $T(n, k, t)$ is the smallest total duration of a star schedule, where the total duration of a schedule is the sum of the durations of its steps. If no star schedule exists (for example when $n \ge 1$ and $k = 0$ or $t = 0$), then $T(n, k, t) = 0$ by convention.

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
